messages.body_plain:
Dear Zixuan Chen,

The problem is in the mcera5 package, so an issue for Dave Klinges to fix. But I traced it to the mcera5:::nc_to_df internal function. If you source the modified version below after loading the mcera5 package that should get you back up and running.

All the best,
Mike

nc_to_df <- function (nc, long, lat, start_time, end_time, dtr_cor = TRUE, dtr_cor_fac = 1) { dat <- tidync::tidync(nc) %>% tidync::hyper_filter(longitude = longitude == long, latitude = latitude == lat) %>% tidync::hyper_tibble() %>% dplyr::mutate(., obs_time = lubridate::ymd_hms("1900:01:01 00:00:00") + (time * 3600), timezone = lubridate::tz(obs_time)) %>% dplyr::filter(., obs_time >= start_time & obs_time < end_time + 1) %>% dplyr::rename(., pressure = sp) %>% dplyr::mutate(., temperature = t2m - 273.15, lsm = dplyr::case_when(lsm < 0 ~ 0, lsm >= 0 ~ lsm), temperature = dplyr::case_when(dtr_cor == TRUE ~ coastal_correct(temperature, lsm, dtr_cor_fac), dtr_cor == FALSE ~ temperature), humidity = humfromdew(d2m - 273.15, temperature, pressure), windspeed = sqrt(u10^2 + v10^2), windspeed = windheight(windspeed, 10, 2), winddir = (atan2(u10, v10) * 180/pi + 180)%%360, cloudcover = tcc * 100, netlong = abs( avg_snlwrf ) * 0.0036, downlong = msdwlwrf * 0.0036, uplong = netlong + downlong, emissivity = downlong/uplong, jd = julday(lubridate::year(obs_time), lubridate::month(obs_time), lubridate::day(obs_time)), si = siflat(lubridate::hour(obs_time), lat, long, jd, merid = 0)) %>% dplyr::mutate(., rad_dni = fdir * 1e-06, rad_glbl = ssrd * 1e-06, rad_glbl = rad_calc(rad_glbl, obs_time, long, lat), rad_dni = rad_calc(rad_dni, obs_time, long, lat), rad_dif = rad_glbl - rad_dni * si) %>% dplyr::mutate(., szenith = 90 - solalt(lubridate::hour(obs_time), lat, long, jd, merid = 0)) %>% dplyr::select(., obs_time, temperature, humidity, pressure, windspeed, winddir, emissivity, cloudcover, netlong, uplong, downlong, rad_dni, rad_dif, szenith, timezone) return(dat) }

messages.subject_clean: Micro_era5: Issue with running model; missing era5 variables
messages.body_plain:
Sorry to bother you, but I’ve solved the problem. I used Python with xarray to change the variable names 'avg_snlwrf' and 'avg_sdlwrf' back to 'msnlwrf' and 'msdwlwrf'.
The code helps:
import xarray as xr
import os

# 文件路径和年份范围
base_path = "F:/swot/34"
years = range(2000, 2011)

# 变量重命名映射
rename_dict = {
    "avg_snlwrf": "msnlwrf",
    "avg_sdlwrf": "msdwlwrf"
}

# 遍历年份
for year in years:
    file_path = os.path.join(base_path, f"34_era5_{year}.nc")
    new_file = os.path.join(base_path, f"34_era5_{year}_renamed.nc <http://renamed.nc>")

    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        print(f"文件 {file_path} 不存在，跳过处理。")
        continue

    # 打开 NetCDF 文件
    ds = xr.open_dataset(file_path)

    # 变量重命名
    ds = ds.rename(rename_dict)

    # 保存为新文件
    ds.to_netcdf(new_file, format="NETCDF4")

    print(f"年份 {year} 变量重命名完成！新的文件: {new_file}")

messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,
It's possibly not there for species that had no length data. Check here to see if that's indeed the case. del_M is just a way to go from whatever the chosen length measure is (e.g., could be head width, SVL) to structural length. So you could independently work it out if you had independent length data for your organism.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: micro_era5() for complex terrain microclimate modelling
messages.subject_clean: micro_era5() for complex terrain microclimate modelling
messages.body_plain:
Hello Michael,

I am currently working on complex mountain terrains, where I have empirical temperature data recorded by HOBO sensors placed 90 cm above the ground. These sensors are positioned in the alpine zone. My objective is to use the micro_era5() function to estimate temperatures at each sensor location and compare them with my field measurements during the 2024 summer season.

For now, I have kept most function parameters at their default values. The DEM resolution is set to 25m, and I have included the CAD effects in the calculations.

However, I have noticed that the model struggles to accurately capture nighttime temperatures and extreme warm conditions. This led me to question whether there might be an issue with the radiation calculations. After reading discussions in the NicheMapR group, I found that the hori parameter is necessary for integrating the effects of terrain shading.

To address this, I ran micro_era5() while specifying the horizon vector for each logger location, as required. However, when comparing the results of models with and without the hori parameter, I found only minimal or no differences at all, at least for TALOC, SOLR, and TSKYC in metout and shadmet outputs.

Below, I have included the micro_era5() function code I used for my models. I can provide additional details if needed.

Would you have any insights into the possible reasons for these results? I would greatly appreciate any guidance on refining my approach or better understanding how the model handles terrain-related variations.

Thank you in advance for your time and for developing this valuable tool.

Emilie

Here is my code :

#--- INPUTS ----

year <- 2024
dstart <- paste0("01/01/", year) # start date #DD/MM/YYYY
dfinish <- paste0("31/08/", year) # end date #DD/MM/YYYY
Usrhyt <- 0.9

messages.body_plain:
Hi Emilie,

You shouldn't see a strong effect of horizon angle on 90 cm air temps (your height for TALOC) - there would be stronger effects closer to the ground (you should see strong effects on the the soil surface temperature - have a look and see). You should see effects on the solar radiation early and late in the day and an overall effect on TSKYC ... e.g. try this to see what I mean:

long <- 6.12223 lat <- 45.22324
slope <- 21.31131 aspect <- 118.1416 horizon <- c(40.206009,41.638817,31.115494,20.940985,15.510981,9.760770,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,7.108164,23.505644,32.918053,35.221779,34.820778,40.807129,42.284172,39.211670,43.772758)

micro<-micro_global(loc = c(long, lat), slope = slope, aspect = aspect)
metout1<-as.data.frame(micro$metout)
micro<-micro_global( loc = c(long, lat), hori = horizon, slope = slope, aspect = aspect )
metout2<-as.data.frame(micro$metout)
plot(metout1$SOLR,type= 'l')
points(metout2$SOLR, type='l',col=2)
plot(metout1$TSKYC,type='l') points(metout2$TSKYC, type='l', col=2)

The most likely issue with the overall mismatch you're getting is that the ERA5 data is not quite up to matching conditions in the complex terrain you're working in, where there can be very strong local effects on wind speed and, as you mention, cold air drainage. I am not sure the cold air drainage corrections of microclima are working properly - see if you get any difference with them turned on vs. off. It may be that some work can be done on improving how the CAD is calculated (check out the details of what the CAD correction does by reading the documentation of the microclima package).

All the best,
Mike
